idiom_name: sealed interface Result<T, E> + record Success/Failure + pattern switch
implementation_notes: Java has no Result in the standard library and its native error channel is exceptions (checked ones even put the failure in the signature), so the pattern is hand-written. Since Java 17 the language has the pieces: a sealed interface Result<T, E> permits record Success<T, E>(T value) and record Failure<T, E>(E error), and a pattern switch over the sealed hierarchy is checked for exhaustiveness (Java 21) - the compiler then enforces the both-cases-handled property that Rust gets from match. Add map/flatMap/orElse helpers or a Match method so chains read as pipelines, and convert exceptions at the boundary where they are thrown. On Java 17 alone the same shape is consumed with pattern instanceof chains; checked exceptions remain idiomatic for failures a caller cannot prevent, which is why this needs a deliberate convention rather than a compiler default.
pitfalls: Exhaustive switch over a sealed hierarchy requires the pattern-switch feature (Java 21); with Java 17 the same code needs instanceof chains, and a forgotten branch falls through silently.
Case patterns must repeat the selector's type arguments (Result.Success<Integer, String>); a dedicated non-generic Result per use, or a non-generic error type, removes the noise.
Records give component-wise equality, but a failure value that is an exception compares by reference; error equality must come from the error type.

variants.name: vavr Either/Try (Java 8 library)
variants.implementation_notes: Vavr is an object-functional extension for Java 8 whose control package supplies the two-case values directly: Either<L, R>, conventionally read as Left = failure and Right = success, with map/flatMap so a chain short-circuits on the failure branch, Try<T> for capturing exceptions at the boundary, and a fold for terminal handling; the project describes itself as providing functional abstractions for error handling on Java 8 (naming Either/Try is analysis of that API, not a quote). It brings the railway to codebases that cannot move past Java 8 at the price of a library dependency whose types cross module boundaries - translate at the module edge as with any framework, and choose it over hand-rolled records where vavr is already in the stack.
variants.idiom_name: Either<L, R> / Try<T> with map/flatMap and fold
pitfalls: Vavr types must not leak into interfaces shared with non-vavr modules, or the dependency becomes transitive; convert to the domain Result at the boundary.
flatMap over Either short-circuits on Left, so a step that returns Try or a plain value needs an explicit conversion (toEither/toTry) before it can join the chain.
